cues.en: If you get hold of two magnets and you push them, you can feel this pushing between them. Turn around the other way and they slam together. Now, what is it, the feeling between those two magnets?
cues.zh: 假如你拿起两块磁铁，把它们推到一起，你能感受到它们之间的这种推力。换个方向，它们就会啪地吸在一起。那么，这两块磁铁之间的那种感觉，到底是什么？

cues.en: What do you mean what's the feeling
cues.zh: 什么叫“到底是什么感觉”

cues.en: two magnets? There's something there, isn't there? I mean that the sensation is that there's something there when you push these two magnets together. Listen to my question. What is the meaning when you say that there's that there's a feeling? Of course you feel it. Now what do you want to know?
cues.zh: 两块磁铁？那里确实有某种东西，不是吗？我是说，当你把这两块磁铁推到一起时，感觉上就是有某种东西在那里。听我的问题。你说“有一种感觉”，这是什么意思？你当然感觉得到。那你还想知道什么？

cues.en: What I want to know is what's going on
cues.zh: 我想知道的是，到底发生了什么

cues.en: between these two bits
cues.zh: 在这两块

cues.en: of metal. The magnets repel each other.
cues.zh: 金属之间。磁铁互相排斥。

cues.en: Then what does
cues.zh: 那这

cues.en: that mean? Or why are they doing that? Or how are they doing it?
cues.zh: 意味着什么？或者它们为什么会这样？或者它们是怎么做到的？

cues.en: You're asking... I must say, I think that's a perfectly reasonable question. Of course, it's a reason. It's an excellent question.
cues.zh: 你问的是……我得说，我觉得这是个完全合理的问题。当然，这是个有理由的问题。这是个极好的问题。

cues.en: Okay?
cues.zh: 明白吗？

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: the problem that you're asking... You see, when you ask why something happens,
cues.zh: 你问的这个问题……你看，当你问一件事为什么发生时，

cues.en: how does a person answer why something happens?
cues.zh: 一个人该怎么回答一件事为什么发生？

cues.en: For example,
cues.zh: 比如说，

cues.en: Aunt Minnie is in the hospital. Why?
cues.zh: 明妮阿姨住院了。为什么？

cues.en: Because she slipped... She went out and she slipped on the ice and broke her hip.
cues.zh: 因为她滑倒了……她出门在冰上滑倒，摔断了髋骨。

cues.en: That satisfies people.
cues.zh: 这就能让人满意了。

cues.en: It satisfies... But it wouldn't satisfy someone who came from another planet, knew nothing about things. At first, don't understand why when you break your hip, do you go to the hospital?
cues.zh: 这能让人满意……但这不会让一个来自另一个星球、对一切一无所知的人满意。首先，他们不明白，为什么你摔断了髋骨，就要去医院？

cues.en: How do you get to the hospital with the... When the hip is broken? Well, because her husband, seeing that she had the hip was broken, called the hospital up and sent somebody to get her. All that is understood by people.
cues.zh: 你怎么带她去医院……髋部骨折的时候？因为她丈夫看到她髋部骨折了，就打电话给医院，派人去接她。这些人们都能理解。

cues.en: Now when you explain a a why,
cues.zh: 现在，当你解释一个“为什么”时，

cues.en: you have to be in some framework that you allow something to be true.
cues.zh: 你必须处在某个框架里，允许某些事情为真。

cues.en: Otherwise, you're perpetually asking why. Why did the husband call up the hospital?
cues.zh: 否则，你就会没完没了地问为什么。丈夫为什么打电话给医院？

cues.en: Because husband is interested in his wife's well fare.
cues.zh: 因为丈夫关心妻子的安危。

cues.en: Not always, some husbands aren't interested in their wife's well for their drunk and they're angry.
cues.zh: 也不总是这样，有些丈夫不关心妻子，因为他们喝醉了，还在生气。

cues.en: And so you begin to get a very interesting understanding of the world and all its complications in order to to... If you try to follow anything up, you go deeper and deeper in various directions.
cues.zh: 于是你开始对这个世界及其所有复杂性获得非常有趣的理解，为了……如果你试图追问任何事情，你会在各个方向上越挖越深。

cues.en: If... For example, you could go, why did she slip on the ice? Well, ice is slippery. Everybody knows that. No problem.
cues.zh: 如果……比如，你可以问，她为什么在冰上滑倒了？嗯，冰很滑。大家都知道。没问题。

cues.en: But you ask, why is ice slippery?
cues.zh: 但你问，冰为什么滑？

cues.en: That's kinda curious. Ice is extremely slippery. It's very interesting.
cues.zh: 这就有点奇怪了。冰极其滑。这非常有意思。

cues.en: You say how does it work?
cues.zh: 你说，这是怎么回事？

cues.en: You could you see, you could either say I'm satisfied that you've answered me ice is slippery that explains it or you go on and say, why is ice slippery?
cues.zh: 你看，你可以要么说，我满意了，你回答了我冰很滑，这就解释了，要么你继续问，冰为什么滑？

cues.en: And then you're involved with something because there aren't many things as slippery as ice.
cues.zh: 然后你就卷入了某些事情，因为没多少东西像冰那么滑。

cues.en: It's very hard to get greasy
cues.zh: 很难找到油腻的

cues.en: stuff, but that's sort of wet and slimy.
cues.zh: 东西，但那有点湿滑黏腻。

cues.en: But a solid that's so slippery
cues.zh: 但固体怎么会这么滑

cues.en: Because it is in the case of ice that when you stand on it, they say,
cues.zh: 因为有人说，站在冰上时，

cues.en: momentarily the pressure melts the ice a little bit so you got a sort of instantaneous
cues.zh: 瞬间的压力会让冰稍微融化，于是你就像是在一层瞬时形成的

cues.en: water surface on which you're slipping.
cues.zh: 水面上打滑。

cues.en: Why on ice and not on other things? Because ice expands when it... Water expands when it freezes so the pressure tries to undo the expansion and melts it. It's capable of melting it, but other substances contract
cues.zh: 为什么偏偏是冰，而不是其他东西？因为冰在……水结冰时会膨胀，所以压力会试图抵消这种膨胀，把冰融化。冰确实会被融化，但其他物质在结冰时会收缩，

cues.en: when they're freezing and when you push them they're just as satisfied to be solid.
cues.zh: 你推它们时，它们还是很乐意保持固态。

cues.en: Why does water expand when it freezes and other substances don't expand when they freeze? Alright? I'm I'm not answering your question, but I'm telling you how difficult the why question is. You have to know what it is that you're permitted to understand
cues.zh: 为什么水结冰时会膨胀，而其他物质结冰时不会？好吧，我并没有回答你的问题，但我是在告诉你，“为什么”这个问题有多难。你得知道哪些东西是你能够理解的，

cues.en: and allowed to be understood and known and what it is you're not.
cues.zh: 哪些东西是允许被理解和知晓的，以及哪些不是。

cues.en: You'll notice in this example that the more I ask why,
cues.zh: 你会注意到，在这个例子中，我问得越多“为什么”，

cues.en: it gets interesting after that's my idea. The deeper thing is the more interesting it is.
cues.zh: 事情就越有意思，这就是我的意思。越深入，就越有意思。

cues.en: And we
cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: could even go further and say, why did she fall down when she slipped?
cues.zh: 甚至还可以继续问：她为什么会在打滑后摔倒？

cues.en: That has to do with gravity, involves in all the planets and everything else. Never mind, It goes on and on. Now when you ask for example,
cues.zh: 这就涉及重力，涉及所有行星以及其他一切。别管了，这个问题会没完没了。现在，比如当你问：

cues.en: why two magnets repel?
cues.zh: 为什么两个磁铁会互相排斥？

cues.en: There are many different levels. It depends on whether you're a student of physics or an ordinary person who doesn't know anything or not. If you're somebody who doesn't know anything at all about it, all I can say that there is a magnetic force that makes them repel and that you're feeling that thought.
cues.zh: 这里有很多不同的层次。要看你是物理学学生，还是一个什么都不懂的普通人。如果你完全不了解这方面，我只能说，存在一种让它们相互排斥的磁力，而你能感受到这种作用。

cues.en: You say, but that's very strange because I don't feel kind of force like that in other circumstances.
cues.zh: 你可能会说，这太奇怪了，因为在其他情况下我从没感受过这种力。

cues.en: When you turn them the other way they attract.
cues.zh: 把它们反过来，它们就会相互吸引。

cues.en: There's a very analogous force, electrical force, is the same kind of a question and you say that's also very weird.
cues.zh: 还有一种非常相似的力，就是电力，也是同样的问题，你也会觉得这很不可思议。

cues.en: But you're not at all disturbed by the fact that when you put your hand on the chair it pushes you back.
cues.zh: 但当你把手放在椅子上，椅子把你推回来时，你却一点也不觉得奇怪。

cues.en: But we found out by looking at it that's the same force as a matter of fact, the electrical force not magnetic exactly in that case, but it's the same electric repulsions that are involved in keeping
cues.zh: 但仔细探究后我们会发现，实际上这是同一种力，严格来说在那时是电力而不是磁力，但正是这种电斥力阻止了

cues.en: your finger away from the chair because everything's made out of its electrical forces in minor and microscopic details.
cues.zh: 你的手指穿透椅子，因为微观细节上，世间万物都是由电力构成的。

cues.en: There's other forces involved, but this is connected
cues.zh: 虽然还涉及其他力，但这都与

cues.en: to electrical forces. It turns out that the magnetic and the electric force with which I wish to explain these things, this this repulsion in the first place, is what ultimately is the deeper
cues.zh: 电力相关。事实证明，我想用来解释这些现象——也就是最初这种排斥现象——的磁力和电力，最终正是更深层的

cues.en: thing that we have to start, that we can start with to explain many other things that looked like they were...
cues.zh: 基础，我们可以从它出发，来解释许多看似……

cues.en: Everybody would just accept them. You know you can't put your hand through the chair,
cues.zh: 大家习以为常的事情。大家都知道手穿不透椅子，

cues.en: That's taken for granted,
cues.zh: 这被视为理所当然，

cues.en: but that you can't put your hand through the chair when looked at more closely why
cues.zh: 但如果仔细探究为什么手穿不透椅子，

cues.en: it involves the same repulsive forces
cues.zh: 就会发现它涉及的排斥力，

cues.en: that appear in magnets.
cues.zh: 其实和磁铁里的排斥力是同一种。

cues.en: The situation you then have to explain is why at magnets it goes over a bigger distance than an ordinarily
cues.zh: 那么你需要解释的反而是，为什么磁力的作用距离比平时大得多，

cues.en: and there it has to do with the fact that in iron all the electrons are spinning in the same direction they all get lined up and they magnify the effect of the force until it's large enough at a distance that you can feel it.
cues.zh: 这和铁的特性有关：所有电子都朝同一个方向自旋，它们整齐排列，放大了力的效应，直到在一定距离之外也足够大，能让你感受到。

cues.en: But it's a force which is present
cues.zh: 但这是一种始终存在的力

cues.en: all the time and very common and is in a basic force of almost, I mean I can go a little further back if I were more technical.
cues.zh: 而且非常普遍，几乎是一种基本的力。我要是更专业一点，还能再往前讲一些。

cues.en: But in the early level I just have to tell you that gonna be one of the things you'll just have to take as an element in the world the existence of magnetic repulsion or electrical
cues.zh: 但在初级阶段，我只能告诉你们，你们得把磁斥力或电斥力、电吸引力的存在，当作世界的一个基本要素来接受

cues.en: or electrical attraction, magnetic attraction.
cues.zh: 或者说电吸引力、磁吸引力。

cues.en: I can't explain that attraction in terms of anything else that's familiar to you.
cues.zh: 我没办法用你们熟悉的任何其他东西来解释这种吸引力。

cues.en: For example, if we say the magnets attract like as if they were connected by rubber bands, I would be cheating you
cues.zh: 比如说，如果我说磁铁相吸就像是被橡皮筋连在一起，那就是在骗你们

cues.en: because they're not connected by rubber bands. I shouldn't be in trouble.
cues.zh: 因为它们并不是被橡皮筋连着的。我不该给自己惹麻烦。

cues.en: You soon ask me about the nature of the band.
cues.zh: 你们很快就会追问橡皮筋的本质是什么。

cues.en: And secondly,
cues.zh: 其次，

cues.en: if you were curious enough, you'd ask me why rubber bands tend to pull back together again and I would end up explaining that in terms of electrical forces,
cues.zh: 如果你们足够好奇，就会问我为什么橡皮筋总想缩回去，而我最后只能用电力来解释，

cues.en: which are the very things that I'm trying to use the rubber bands to explain. So I have cheated very badly, you see.
cues.zh: 而电力恰恰是我本想用橡皮筋来解释的东西。你看，我这就骗得很离谱了。

cues.en: So I'm not going to be able to give you an answer to why magnets attract each other except to tell you that they do
cues.zh: 所以我没办法回答磁铁为什么相互吸引，只能告诉你们它们确实相吸

cues.en: and to tell you that that's one of the elements in the world of different kinds of forces. There are electrical forces, magnetic forces, gravitational forces, and others,
cues.zh: 并且告诉你们，这是世界上各种力中的一个要素。有电力、磁力、引力，还有其他力，

cues.en: and those are some of the parts.
cues.zh: 这些就是其中的一部分。

cues.en: If you were a student you go fur... I could go further. I could tell you that the magnetic forces are related to the electrical forces very intimately.
cues.zh: 如果你是学生，你会走得更……我还可以再深入一点。我可以告诉你，磁力与电力的关系非常密切。

cues.en: That our relationship between the gravity forces and electrical forces remains unknown
cues.zh: 重力与电力之间的关系仍是未知的

cues.en: and so on.
cues.zh: 诸如此类。

cues.en: But I really can't do a good job,
cues.zh: 但我真的没法很好地

cues.en: any job,
cues.zh: 用任何方式

cues.en: of explaining magnetic force in terms of something else that you're more familiar with because I don't understand it in terms of anything else that you're more familiar with.
cues.zh: 用你更熟悉的别的东西来解释磁力，因为我本人也没法用你更熟悉的别的东西来理解它。
